anomalies.GEN.1135: Train 6 (epoch 128, about 4:10 AM EDT 10-31) moved this share. The class epoch (GEN.1135 retires Class Q, GEN.1136 raises the Class V line from 1.25 g to 2 g, GEN.1142 adds the class lines and Class E) re-derives every planet class, and the same train changed the halo mass function (GEN.1154), ocean tides (GEN.1034), ring ages (GEN.1057), day and night state (GEN.1097), the resonance capture draw (GEN.1172), giant tilts (GEN.1165), star spin (GEN.1163, GEN.1170) and the close-binary period trend (GEN.705). The ranges stay until the planet and star chains settle; re-baseline after the last 8.1 train (TEST.430).
anomalies.GEN.1160: Trains 8 and 9 (epochs 130 and 131, merged 11:59 PM EDT 10-31 and 4:10 PM EST 11-04) moved the class of moons: GEN.1160 gives Class D and Class C by the roundness ratio and makes the small unrounded bodies an Asteroid type with no class letter, so Class C is gone from every moon cell (0 against 0.3 to 0.5) and Class D rose to 0.7 to 0.9. An intended change, not a fault; the moon ranges stay until the planet chains settle. TEST.656 (11-06): G2V cold moons are 0.894 Class D (42 of 47) against 0.806; the same shift.
anomalies.GEN.1244: Train 10 (epoch 132, merged 7:11 AM EST 11-05) moved the moon populations: GEN.1244 forms the regular moons of a giant in the disk zone between the corotation radius and 30 planet radii, and GEN.1111 gives a rogue planet its moons by the same chain. Class D of cold K5V and ecosphere M2V moons rose past the range (0.799 against 0.796; 0.851 against 0.707) and two ceilings of moons rose by a few hundredths (K5V hot unlimited 0.064 against 0.062; M2V ecosphere microbial 0.085 against 0.068). An intended change, not a fault; the moon ranges stay until the planet chains settle.
anomalies.GEN.728: Train 4 (epoch 126, 3:40 PM EDT 10-30) moved this share. The planet architecture (GEN.728, GEN.729, GEN.730, GEN.828, GEN.829, GEN.920) now sets the planet count, spacing, belts and giants of every system, with the snow line and ice from Lodders (GEN.950), the greenhouse table (GEN.850) and rocky bodies made again at the star's final age (GEN.992). The ranges are the post-cut-over (GEN.646) ones and stay until the planet and star chains settle; re-baseline after the last 8.1 train (TEST.430). TEST.656 (11-06): the A0V moon Class B shares (5 of 24 at the ecosphere, 2 of 11 hot) are impact moons of heavy planets (2 to 11 Earth masses) and follow the planet Class B share of the same cells (0.12 and 0.26 against 0.062 and 0.156), so they are this fault, not a second one.
anomalies.GEN.746: an intended change, not a fault: the dose laws rebuilt from measured data (GEN.746, GEN.747, GEN.748) put the radiation of an airless moon in the Red tier, so a K5V moon that Temperature alone left Yellow (about 17 of 100) is now Red; the shares are the post-cut-over measurement and wait for the re-baseline after the train
anomalies.GEN.819: Trains 8 and 9 (epochs 130 and 131, merged 11:59 PM EDT 10-31 and 4:10 PM EST 11-04) moved these shares with the giants chain (GEN.819, GEN.821, GEN.824, GEN.784), belt birth (GEN.1068 b, GEN.1156), the clearance ledger (GEN.1014), the disk gas law (GEN.999), the ocean cover law (GEN.1147), the several-life-classes air (GEN.1209, GEN.1213), the capped greenhouse and steam air (GEN.1236, GEN.1238, GEN.1240) and the disk infall (GEN.1242): the cells flagged are listed by the census itself and moved by a few percentage points of a class, not in kind. The ranges stay until the planet and star chains settle; re-baseline after the last 8.1 train (TEST.430).
anomalies.GEN.829: class T (gas dwarf) is never drawn: no 2 to 20 Earth-mass sub-Neptune population exists (GEN.829); the pre-cut-over spine drew it almost never either
anomalies.GEN.941: Train 3 (epoch 125, 7:27 AM EDT 10-30) moved this share. Every census cell is a forced star type, and forced types are now stars of the population model (GEN.941; their mass, age and metallicity come from the tracks of GEN.935 and the mass function of GEN.927 to GEN.930, not from the hand-made letter ranges), the spectral letters follow the Pecaut and Mamajek table (GEN.943), giants settle at the final age (GEN.961) and a world gets no life class before its first life step (GEN.1001). The ranges are the post-cut-over (GEN.646) ones and stay until the star and planet chains settle; re-baseline after the last 8.1 train (TEST.430).
anomalies.TEST.656: Train 12 (epoch 134, merged 2:42 PM EST 11-06) cut the moon census to a few bodies: GEN.1082 to GEN.1084 put captured moons in the irregular store, which the census does not read, so a rocky planet's `moons` holds only the moons of a giant impact (a 1 in 12 draw) or a binary capture, 24 moons in 300 planets at A0V ecosphere, 11 hot, 1 at M2V ecosphere, 5 at K5V hot, against 500 to 700 in the reference. The moon ranges are those of the reference's population, and a share of 8 to 24 bodies swings by 0.1 to 0.2, so the K5V ecosphere unlimited share (1 of 8) and the M2V cold microbial and none shares (7 of 78, 0.090 against 0.077) are sampling width, not a change in the bodies. The M2V hot moon cell is empty by physics: 15 of its 300 planets (orbits of 0.03 to 0.12 AU, spin periods of 4 to 29 h) were born with a moon and the tide brought 12 of them down onto the planet (`fallen_moons`, GEN.959) and the rest were lost, so no moon remains. Re-baseline the moon ranges after the last 8.1 train (TEST.430), with the census reading the irregular moons.
anomalies.GEN.1327: Train 13 (epoch 135, merged 1:03 AM EST 11-07) moved three shares just past a range that is itself a 95 percent bound of an earlier run: A0V and F5V ecosphere planets with an unlimited life ceiling (0.223 against 0.232 and 0.167 against 0.188 at 300 draws, one standard deviation of a share this size is about 0.025) and G2V hot planets in Class C (0.120 against 0.119). GEN.1282 re-orders the draws of the deferred climate and GEN.1304 warms temperate wet worlds, so these cells reshuffle; the sweep letters were checked on resamples (reports/gen1327-sweep-life-letters-2026-11-07.md) and the capable share did not move. A sampling-sized shift, not a fault; the ranges stay until the re-baseline after the last 8.1 train (TEST.660).
anomalies.GEN.1338: Train 14 (epoch 136, merged 5:24 AM EST 11-07) moved seven planet shares just past a range that is a 95 percent bound of an earlier run, in both directions: F5V ecosphere planets in Class N (0.110 against 0.166), G2V ecosphere planets in Class E (0.143 against 0.138) and with no life ceiling (0.623 against 0.611), K0III ecosphere planets with no ceiling (0.697 against 0.673), M2V cold planets in Class J (0.083 against 0.062), G2V cold planets with an unlimited ceiling (1 body in 207 against a floor of 0.005) and G2V hot planets with no Yellow tier (none in 300 against a floor of 0.003). Each census draws 300 planets a cell on a new random stream after a train that moves draws (GEN.1282), and the edges of the ranges are 95 percent bounds, so a share sits just past an edge in a few cells each time; the cells that were flagged after train 13 went back inside (6 of 11), as they are expected to. A sampling-sized shift, not a fault; the ranges stay until the re-baseline after the last 8.1 train (TEST.660). The three moon flags are cells of 3 to 14 moons and carry TEST.656.
anomalies.GEN.1353: Trains 15 to 18 (epochs 137 to 140, merged 11-07 to 10:45 AM EST 11-08) moved 17 shares of the class census past a range. Nine are moon shares in cells where moons are few since train 12 (TEST.656): Class D too common in A0V ecosphere (0.739 against 0.670), A0V hot (0.900 against 0.657), F5V cold (0.884 against 0.870) and M2V hot moons (1.000 against 0.720, with Class C absent), and the life ceiling in F5V cold moons (microbial 0.041 against a floor of 0.104, none 0.959 against 0.895), F5V hot moons (none 0.955 against 0.878), G2V cold moons (no microbial ceiling, floor 0.0015) and G2V hot moons (none 0.750 against a floor of 0.817). Eight are planet shares: A0V ecosphere planets in the Red tier (0.591 against a floor of 0.625), the Yellow tier (0.396 against 0.371) and with a microbial ceiling (0.100 against 0.073), F5V ecosphere planets with no life ceiling (0.902 against 0.736), F5V hot planets with a microbial ceiling (0.062 against 0.040), A0V cold planets with no Class V (floor 0.012) and G2V ecosphere planets with no Class N (floor 0.010). The F5V ecosphere no-ceiling share is the one large move. The likely source is GEN.1397 (life is decided by conditions and the habitable request no longer redraws a body), with GEN.1398 and GEN.1399 and the new draws of epochs 137 to 140, but it is not isolated to one item. The ranges are 95 percent bounds of a 300-draw reference on a stream that moves with every train (GEN.1282), so a few shares sit past an edge each time. 18 tags whose range holds again are removed. A tag, not a fault; the ranges stay until the re-baseline after the last 8.1 train (TEST.660), which also decides whether the F5V share is a fault.
anomalies.GEN.1537: Train 22 (epoch 144, merged 11:03 AM EST 11-11) and the earlier trains since the last re-tag moved 18 shares of the class census past a range, all in small cells and none a cell that draws nothing: the census now draws every cell around a lone star (BINARY_SYSTEM off), because with a companion the other star's light (GEN.1441) put the planets of the A0V cold and F5V ecosphere cells into the hot zone and emptied five cells. The moon ceilings are few-body cells (A0V cold, F5V ecosphere and hot, K5V ecosphere, M2V cold and hot), the planet tiers Red and Yellow are a few points past their ranges (G2V cold, K0III cold, K5V hot, where Yellow is absent against a floor of 0.024), the ceiling unlimited is absent in K5V cold planets, and two class shares are just over their top (G2V ecosphere Class C 0.190 against 0.138, K0III ecosphere Class E 0.123 against 0.106). No fault was found; the ranges stay until the TEST.660 re-baseline after the last 8.1 train.
